title: About HART
lede: HART Railroad is an HO scale model railroad set on Neville Island, the industrial island in the Ohio River just below Pittsburgh.

sections.heading: The island
paragraphs: Neville Island was farmland until about 1900. Within a generation it had furnaces, coke ovens and chemical plants, nearly all of them shipping by rail, with barges working the river alongside.

For nearly a century the Pittsburgh & Ohio Valley switched those plants and handed their cars to the larger roads, until it shut down in 1994. Much of what we know about it comes from the people who worked it, and their stories are a big part of why this layout exists.

sections.heading: East end industries
paragraphs: Much of the island's industry traces back to one site at its east end. American Steel & Wire put a blast furnace there around 1900 and built the P&OV to serve it. In 1929 new owners added coke ovens and a cement plant, and by the war years the company was Pittsburgh Coke & Chemical.

The plant worked as one system. Coal went into the ovens and came out as coke for the blast furnaces. Slag left over from making iron was ground into cement, with limestone brought down the river by barge. Gas and tar from the ovens fed a chemical works. During the Second World War the plant also learned to make activated carbon from coal, for gas masks.

In the 1960s the company was broken up and each piece went its own way. The coke and iron went to Shenango, the cement through a run of cement companies to Kosmos, the carbon to Calgon, and the chemicals to U.S. Steel and later Aristech. The furnaces went cold around 1990 and the last coke came out of the ovens in 2016, but cement and carbon still move through the island today.

sections.heading: Our railroad
paragraphs: HART imagines what came after the P&OV. Its Pittsburgh & Chartiers Valley Division takes over the island work, switching Shenango, Kosmos, Calgon and Aristech along with a few of the island's newer customers, and interchanging cars with the nearby railroads.

sections.heading: On this site
paragraphs: History & Industries is for anyone curious about the island. It holds what we have learned about the P&OV and the plants it served, with old photographs, advertisements and clippings credited to their sources where we could find them.
Operations is for the people who come to run trains. It has a primer for first-timers, the paperwork used at the layout, and a look around the layout room and the equipment that works it.
